summary.text: Preet, a new bride, waits for her husband Harry on Karva Chauth, fearing he won't come. She checks her phone, sees no signal, and watches the moon rise. When she finally hears Harry's voice, she learns he is bathing, not at home. The script ends with her lowering her chhanni as the diya flickers out, leaving the question of whether she will believe him or not.

items.one_line_summary: Preet waits for Harry on Karva Chauth, fearing he won't come, as the moon rises and her phone finally connects to him.
items.ending_rationale: The ending resolves Preet's anxiety with a phone call, satisfying closure but lacking emotional or plot escalation to drive viewer engagement.

emotion.narrative: The morning scene (L1-L7) opens with joy and trust as Preet and Beeji share a warm, familiar bond, with Beeji expressing faith in Harry's return (L7). The sangeet (L8-L17) amplifies joy and surprise as the women laugh and celebrate, with Dolly's teasing (L10) and the jaggo procession (L16) creating a vibrant, communal energy. As the moon rises (L18-L27), fear and sadness grow as Preet waits in silence, her dry lips (L26) and the empty stairs (L26) reflect her anxiety and isolation. The phone call (L28-L31) brings relief and joy, with Preet's voice (L29) confirming Harry's presence, ending with a flicker of hope as the diya dies (L31).

targets.fit_rationale: The script contains several regional and cultural references that require adaptation for a Hindi-speaking audience, especially in idioms and food terms. While the core festival rituals are recognizable, the humor and speech patterns are Punjabi-specific and may not translate well without modification.

issues.explanation: 'Sargi' and 'mathri' are regional foods not widely recognized in Hindi-speaking markets; 'sargi' is a specific Punjabi dish, and 'mathri' is a term used in rural Punjab but not standard in Hindi cuisine.
'Puttar' is a colloquial term for daughter-in-law in Punjabi, not used in standard Hindi; it may be perceived as disrespectful or outdated in a Hindi audience.

'Naach na jaane aangan tedha, Pai ji!' is a Punjabi-origin idiom with humor and regional flavor; 'Pai ji' is a respectful term for elder, but 'aangan tedha' is not idiomatic in Hindi and may not translate well to a Hindi audience.

targets.fit_rationale: The script contains multiple culture-specific rituals, foods, and honorifics that are not part of Tamil cultural lexicon. While the core emotional arc is universal, the premise relies on North Indian traditions that have no parallel in Tamil society. Without transcreation, the script would feel alien and disconnected to Tamil audiences.

issues.explanation: Sargi and mathri are North Indian foods not familiar in Tamil households; 'sargi' is a specific dish with no local equivalent and may confuse or alienate Tamil audiences.
'Puttar' is a Hindi term for daughter-in-law, not used in Tamil; it carries a caste-based social weight and is not part of Tamil familial address systems.
'Karva Chauth' and 'sangeet' are rituals from North India; Tamil audience has no cultural memory of these events, making the premise feel foreign and disconnected.
'Naach na jaane aangan tedha, Pai ji!' uses Hindi-style humor and a non-Tamil phrase; 'Pai ji' is a respectful title not used in Tamil kinship structures.
'Shava shava, balle balle' is a Hindi-originated bhangra chant with no Tamil equivalent; it lacks local linguistic rhythm and cultural resonance.
'Jaggo' is a North Indian ritual with no Tamil parallel; the concept of a 'jaggo' procession is unfamiliar and may not resonate with Tamil audience.
'Chhanni' is a North Indian ritual object; Tamil culture uses 'thiruvizha' or 'kuzhali' as marriage symbols, not chhanni.
'Sarson da saag' and 'makki di roti' are North Indian dishes; Tamil audiences are familiar with idli, dosa, filter coffee, not these items.
'Chhanni' is a ritual object used in North Indian weddings; Tamil audience does not recognize this symbol or its function.

comps.differentiator: Script focuses on emotional wait and doubt, not a narrative of love or conflict.

comps.title: Karle Pyaar Karle

comps.differentiator: Script centers on Karva Chauth ritual and emotional tension, not rebellion or games.

comps.title: Farhana (film)

comps.differentiator: Script is ritual-based with moon and waiting, not financial or family crisis.

comps.title: Paper Boy

tropes.name: Scheming in-law
tropes.rationale: Beeji opposes video call, insists face-to-face, showing traditional in-law control over ritual.

tropes.name: Dowry harassment
tropes.rationale: Beeji emphasizes no water, links to bride's hunger, reflects dowry-related pressure on new bride.

tropes.name: Sacrificial love
tropes.rationale: Preet waits, calls repeatedly, shows emotional sacrifice for Harry's return.

tropes.name: Forced marriage
tropes.rationale: Harry's promise, jaggo procession, shows marriage ritual enforced by family expectations.

tropes.name: Hidden identity
tropes.rationale: Jaggi and others perform rituals, suggesting hidden roles in family hierarchy.

tropes.name: Revenge
tropes.rationale: Jassi mocks contractor, shows resistance to family power, hints at hidden anger.

elements.text: INT. DHILLON HAVELI, KITCHEN - DAWN
Still dark outside. PREET (24), a new bride with fresh chooda on her wrists, eats sargi with her mother-in-law BEEJI (62). Mathri, pheniyan, a glass of milk.
Kha le, puttar. Aaj suraj se chaand tak, paani ki ek boond bhi nahi.
elements.speaker: BEEJI

elements.text: Beeji, mera pehla Karva Chauth hai aur aaj hi Bunty ka sangeet bhi. Main nachungi kaise bhookhi?
elements.speaker: PREET

elements.text: Isi liye toh mehendi wale haath sabse sundar lagte hain. Bhookh mein bhi.
elements.speaker: BEEJI

elements.text: Harry ne promise kiya hai, chaand nikalne se pehle aa jayega.
elements.speaker: PREET

elements.text: Mere Harry ka promise? Rab rakha.
elements.speaker: BEEJI

elements.text: EXT. DHILLON HAVELI, COURTYARD - NIGHT
Fairy lights. A dhol. The sangeet is in full swing. Harry's elder brother JASSI (32) tries to dance bhangra and stumbles. His cousin DOLLY (22) shrieks with laughter.
Naach na jaane aangan tedha, Pai ji!
elements.speaker: DOLLY

elements.text: Oye, aangan sach mein tedha hai! Contractor ne paise khaaye!
elements.speaker: JASSI

elements.text: Everyone laughs. The dhol player shouts.
Shava shava! Balle balle!
elements.speaker: DOLLY

elements.text: (checking her phone) Harry ka phone switch off aa raha hai.
elements.speaker: PREET

elements.text: Bhabhi, jaggo nikalne wali hai. Chalo, gaagar uthao!
elements.speaker: DOLLY

elements.text: The women lift a brass gaagar lit with diyas onto Preet's head. The jaggo procession moves through the lane, singing, banging steel plates.
Jaggo aayi aa! Jaagde raho!
elements.speaker: DOLLY

elements.text: INT. DHILLON HAVELI, ROOF - NIGHT
Thali with a diya, a karva of water, and a chhanni. The women wait for the moon. Preet's lips are dry. Beeji holds her hand.
Chaand nikalne wala hai. Harry kahan hai?
elements.speaker: BEEJI

elements.text: Pata nahi, Beeji. Highway pe jam hai, last message mein likha tha.
elements.speaker: PREET

elements.text: Fikar na kar, Preet. Video call pe chhanni se dekh lena.
elements.speaker: JASSI

elements.text: (sharp) Video call pe vrat nahi khulta, Jassi. Mard saamne hona chahiye.
elements.speaker: BEEJI

elements.text: Below, in the kitchen, the smell of sarson da saag and makki di roti rises. Preet hasn't eaten since dawn.
(pointing) Chaand! Chaand aa gaya!
elements.speaker: DOLLY

elements.text: The full moon rises over the rooftops. All the women lift their chhannis. Preet lifts hers, and sees only the empty stairs.
Beeji, ek baar aur try karti hoon.
elements.speaker: PREET

elements.text: She calls. This time the phone rings. Someone answers.
(relieved) Harry! Kahan ho tum? Chaand nikal aaya hai.
elements.speaker: PREET

elements.text: Harry naha raha hai. Aap kaun bol rahi hain?
elements.speaker: WOMAN

elements.text: Preet slowly lowers the chhanni. The diya on her thali flickers out.
